questions.prompt: Making tella at home using grain and yeast is an example of:
options: Traditional biotechnology
Soil conservation
Selective breeding
Photosynthesis
questions.explanation: Using yeast to ferment grain into a drink like tella is traditional biotechnology, a practice that is thousands of years old.

questions.prompt: Which of these is the smallest living unit of the body?
options: An organ
A cell
A tissue
A system
questions.explanation: The cell is the smallest living unit. Cells join to form tissues, then organs, then systems.

questions.prompt: Which sugar is the main food made by a plant during photosynthesis?
options: Lactose
Glucose
Sucrose from the soil
Starch from the air
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis makes glucose, which the plant uses for energy, stores as starch, or uses to grow.

questions.prompt: In which part of the cell are the chromosomes found?
options: The cell membrane
The cytoplasm
The nucleus
The cell wall
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are thread-like structures located inside the nucleus of the cell.

questions.prompt: Throwing factory waste into a river so the water becomes harmful is an example of:
options: Conservation
Reforestation
Pollution
Terracing
questions.explanation: Adding harmful substances to water, air or land is pollution, which damages living things and ecosystems.

questions.prompt: Which organ takes oxygen from the air into the blood?
options: The lungs
The liver
The kidney
The brain
questions.explanation: The lungs are the gas exchange organs of the respiratory system, taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: When yeast respires WITH plenty of oxygen, which products does it make?
options: Ethanol and lactic acid
Carbon dioxide and water
Glucose and oxygen
Methane and starch
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration in yeast uses oxygen to break sugar into carbon dioxide and water, releasing a lot of energy. Ethanol is only made without oxygen.

questions.prompt: What is meant by a pair of homologous chromosomes?
options: Two matching chromosomes, one from each parent
Two chromosomes joined to make a gene
A chromosome copied twice in one cell
A chromosome with no genes on it
questions.explanation: Homologous chromosomes are a matching pair carrying the same genes, with one chromosome inherited from each parent.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of a tissue rather than an organ?
options: The heart
Muscle
The stomach
The kidney
questions.explanation: Muscle is a tissue made of similar cells working together. The heart, stomach and kidney are organs built from several tissues.

questions.prompt: What is the main role of the roots in supplying photosynthesis?
options: They trap light energy
They take in water from the soil
They release oxygen into the air
They make glucose directly
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water from the soil, which is then carried up the xylem to the leaves for photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: How does vaccination help protect a child from a disease such as measles?
options: It cures the disease after the child is very sick
It prepares the body to fight the germ before infection
It kills all bacteria in the air around the child
It replaces the need to ever eat healthy food
questions.explanation: A vaccine trains the body's defences in advance, so it can quickly fight the germ if the child is later exposed to it.

questions.prompt: After aerobic respiration in a muscle cell, which waste gas does the blood carry back to the lungs?
options: Oxygen
Carbon dioxide
Nitrogen
Methane
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide as a waste gas. The blood carries it to the lungs to be breathed out.

questions.prompt: Why is natural gas described as a non-renewable resource?
options: It can be replaced in a few weeks
It is made fresh by plants every season
It took millions of years to form and cannot be quickly replaced
It grows back like a forest
questions.explanation: Natural gas, like coal and oil, formed over millions of years. Once used up it cannot be replaced in a useful time, so it is non-renewable.

questions.prompt: Why is a tej or tella container often kept sealed during fermentation?
options: To let in plenty of fresh oxygen
To keep oxygen out so yeast makes ethanol
To freeze the mixture solid
To give the yeast bright sunlight
questions.explanation: Sealing the container keeps oxygen out, so the yeast respires anaerobically (ferments) and produces the ethanol wanted in the drink.

questions.prompt: Why are brothers and sisters from the same parents not identical to one another?
options: Meiosis mixes the parents' genes differently in each sex cell
Mitosis makes each child slightly different
Children choose their own genes
All children get exactly the same chromosomes
questions.explanation: Meiosis produces sex cells with different combinations of the parents' genes, so each child inherits a unique mix and siblings differ.

questions.prompt: A plant is kept in bright light and warm air but very little carbon dioxide. What is most likely limiting its rate of photosynthesis?
options: Light
Temperature
Carbon dioxide
Water vapour in the air
questions.explanation: When light and warmth are plentiful but carbon dioxide is scarce, carbon dioxide becomes the limiting factor that slows photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: An agricultural centre breeds teff plants over many years, each time keeping seeds only from plants that resisted disease. What is the likely result?
options: Teff plants that are more resistant to disease
Teff that turns into maize
Teff plants with no genes at all
Teff that cannot make seeds
questions.explanation: Selective breeding chooses parents with a wanted feature, so over generations the disease-resistant trait becomes more common in the teff crop.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes what happens in genetic engineering?
options: A useful gene is moved from one organism into another
Two whole animals are bred together over many years
Sugar is fermented into alcohol by yeast
Soil is protected by planting trees on a slope
questions.explanation: Genetic engineering moves a gene from one organism into another, giving it a new characteristic, such as bacteria that make human insulin.

questions.prompt: The order of bases along a gene is important because it acts as the code to:
options: Build a particular protein
Store water in the cell
Make the cell wall thicker
Trap light for photosynthesis
questions.explanation: The sequence of bases in a gene is the instruction the cell reads to build a specific protein, which then helps decide a characteristic.

questions.prompt: A human skin cell with 46 chromosomes divides by mitosis to heal a wound. How many chromosomes are in each new cell?
questions.explanation: Mitosis makes two identical cells, each with the same chromosome number as the parent, so each new skin cell has 46 chromosomes.

questions.prompt: When you run fast, your breathing and heart rate both increase. Why do these two systems speed up together?
options: To deliver more oxygen and glucose to working muscles
To make the muscles stop respiring
To cool the blood down to freezing
To remove all carbon dioxide from food
questions.explanation: Running muscles need more energy, so the respiratory system takes in more oxygen and the circulatory system pumps faster to deliver oxygen and glucose.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly compares photosynthesis and respiration in a plant?
options: Photosynthesis takes in carbon dioxide; respiration releases it
Both processes only happen in the dark
Respiration makes glucose; photosynthesis uses it up
Neither process needs oxygen at any time
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis takes in carbon dioxide and gives out oxygen, while respiration does the opposite, taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide.

questions.prompt: If one species of insect that pollinates a crop disappears, why can this harm the whole ecosystem?
options: Food chains and other species that depend on it are affected
It immediately makes the soil more fertile
It has no effect on any other living thing
It increases the amount of coal in the ground
questions.explanation: Species are linked through food chains and services like pollination, so losing one can disturb many others and damage the whole ecosystem.

questions.prompt: Allowing too many cattle to graze the same grassland until the plants are stripped bare leads to soil erosion mainly because:
options: Bare soil with no plant cover is easily washed or blown away
The cattle add nutrients that wash the soil away
Grass roots make the soil too loose to use
Grazing adds extra topsoil to the land
questions.explanation: Overgrazing removes the plant cover and roots that hold the soil, leaving bare ground that rain and wind can easily erode.

questions.prompt: What would happen to photosynthesis in a leaf cell if it had no chlorophyll at all?
options: Photosynthesis could not happen because light could not be absorbed
Photosynthesis would speed up greatly
The cell would make more glucose than normal
Oxygen would be taken in instead of released
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs the light energy needed for photosynthesis. Without it, the cell cannot capture light, so no photosynthesis takes place.

questions.prompt: Penicillin is grown using a mould in large tanks. Which group of micro-organisms does this antibiotic act against?
options: Bacteria that cause infections
All fungi in the body
Healthy human cells only
Plant cells in the soil
questions.explanation: Penicillin is an antibiotic that kills or stops bacteria, so it is used to treat bacterial infections. It does not work against viruses.

questions.prompt: A town gets its drinking water from a river that is also used as a toilet upstream. Several people fall ill with diarrhoea. Which combination of actions would BEST reduce these illnesses?
options: Build proper latrines away from the river and treat or boil drinking water
Ask people to exercise more and eat less salt
Vaccinate everyone against diabetes
Cut down nearby trees to open up the river
questions.explanation: The illness spreads through water polluted by human waste, so safe sanitation away from the river plus treating or boiling water tackles the real cause.

questions.prompt: Two parents already have three daughters. What is the chance that their next child will be a boy?
options: Almost certain, because they keep having children
About 1 in 2 (50%), because the father can give X or Y
Zero, because they can only have girls
About 1 in 4, because three girls were already born
questions.explanation: Each pregnancy is independent. The father's sperm is equally likely to carry X or Y, so each child has about a 50% chance of being a boy, no matter the earlier children.

questions.prompt: A student counts bubbles of gas given off by a water plant under different brightness of light to study photosynthesis. The gas bubbles are mostly:
options: Oxygen, a product of photosynthesis
Carbon dioxide taken from the water
Nitrogen from the air
Water vapour escaping
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis releases oxygen, so the bubbles are mainly oxygen. Counting them shows how the rate changes as the light gets brighter.

questions.prompt: A company needs to produce a large, pure and reliable supply of a human hormone quickly. Which method is most suitable?
options: Genetic engineering of bacteria to make the hormone
Selective breeding of cattle over many years
Fermenting teff dough with wild yeast
Collecting the hormone from wild animals in a park
questions.explanation: Genetic engineering lets bacteria make an exact human hormone quickly, in large pure amounts, which selective breeding or traditional fermentation cannot do.

questions.prompt: A region wants both firewood and a healthy forest for the future. Which plan best balances using and conserving the forest?
options: Plant new trees regularly and harvest only as fast as they regrow
Cut all the trees now and plant nothing
Ban people from ever entering the forest and stop planting
Allow free, unlimited cutting to meet demand
questions.explanation: Conservation means wise use: replanting and harvesting no faster than the forest regrows lets people use firewood while keeping the forest for the future.

questions.prompt: After a hillside forest is cleared, a downstream village notices its river floods more after heavy rain and runs dry in the dry season. Why does losing the forest cause both problems?
options: Trees normally soak up rain and release water slowly, evening out the flow
Trees normally pump extra water into the river all year
Forests make rivers flow backwards uphill
Removing trees adds more topsoil to slow the water
questions.explanation: Forests soak up rainfall and release it slowly. Without them, rain rushes off causing floods, and little water is stored to feed the river in the dry season.

questions.prompt: A cell divides and produces four cells, each with half the original chromosome number. Which process happened, and where in the body would it occur?
options: Meiosis, in the reproductive organs making sex cells
Mitosis, in healing skin
Fermentation, in the gut
Mitosis, in the reproductive organs
questions.explanation: Producing four cells with half the chromosomes is meiosis, which happens in the reproductive organs to make sex cells (sperm or eggs).

questions.prompt: A doctor describes the stomach as an organ. Which statement best explains why the stomach is called an organ and not a tissue?
options: It is made of several different tissues working together for one function
It is a single type of cell repeated many times
It is smaller than a single cell
It works completely alone with no link to other parts
questions.explanation: An organ is made of different tissues that work together to do a job. The stomach contains muscle, lining and other tissues, so it is an organ.

questions.prompt: A plant makes more glucose than it needs straight away. In what form does it usually store the extra?
options: As ethanol
As starch
As lactic acid
As oxygen gas
questions.explanation: Plants store extra glucose as starch, which can be turned back into glucose later when energy is needed.

questions.prompt: A health worker says heart disease linked to diet cannot be 'caught' from another person. This means heart disease is best classed as:
options: A non-communicable disease
A communicable disease
A disease spread by mosquitoes
A disease spread through dirty water
questions.explanation: Diseases that do not pass from person to person, such as diet-related heart disease and diabetes, are non-communicable diseases.
